slides.title: Former NFL QB Matt Hasselbeck volunteers his brain for CTE research in hopes of finding a diagnosis in the living
slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>Chronic traumatic encephalopathy — CTE — is a debilitating, degenerative brain disease that's been linked to the repeated head trauma that comes with playing football. For now, there's no way to diagnose CTE while someone is alive. Matt Hasselbeck is trying to change that. The former NFL quarterback is working with Boston University in an effort to find a method of discovering CTE in living people. The Associated Press reported on those efforts Wednesday. Per the report,

<<<INDENT>>>(cont) Hasselbeck recently spent two days with Boston University, volunteering his body and brain to undergo a series of tests to determine the extent to which his playing career and the repeated head trauma that came with it has affected his brain health. What Hasselbeck underwent in CTE studyHasselbeck told AP that the tests included a blood sample, an MRI on his brain and a PET (positron emission tomography) scan that injects a radioactive tracer that maps out the brain's function.

<<<INDENT>>>(cont) contaminated drug test go figure how that happened. "On Aug. 12, Keim spoke about the accusations with Trey Wingo on "The Wingo Network" podcast. <<<INDENT>>>(cont) “Coach Chesney is a leader of men,” said Carr, who was at Dodger Stadium on Monday evening and was on the field before the game. “So many guys get hired just based on scheme. slides.title: Hockey Canada extends bans of all but one player acquitted of sexual assault in 2018 case
slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>CALGARY, Alberta (AP) — Three of the five players acquitted of sexual assault in the high-profile 2018 Canada world junior case have had their international play suspensions get extended for at least another year, with only one set for immediate reinstatement. Hockey Canada on Wednesday extended Michael McLeod’s ban from representing the country until Nov. 10, 2030, Dillon Dube through the same date in 2028 and Carter Hart through that date in 2027.

<<<INDENT>>>(cont) Cal Foote’s suspension will end this November, while Alex Formenton has been reinstated. The decisions were announced after an independent appeal board ruled that the players breached Hockey Canada’s code of conduct. Last year, the NHL allowed the players to sign contracts beginning in October and to play in December. slides.title: Former Penguins Prospect Signs In The KHL
slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>A former Pittsburgh Penguins prospect is heading to the KHL. The Shanghai Dragons have signed former Penguins prospect defenseman Calen Addison to a one-year contract. Addison was selected by the Penguins in the second round of the 2018 NHL Entry Draft, 53rd overall. He was once considered one of the Penguins' top prospects, but he never ended up playing a game for Pittsburgh.

<<<INDENT>>>(cont) This is because the Penguins traded Addison to the Minnesota Wild in February 2020 as part of the the trade that brought forward Jason Zucker to Pittsburgh. Addison played in three games for the Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins in 2018-19, however, where he posted two assists. After being traded by the Penguins, Addison played four NHL seasons from 2020-21 to 2023-24.

slides.title: Coachella Valley Firebirds Sign Defenseman Gustav Olofsson
slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>The Coachella Firebirds, the American Hockey League (AHL) Seattle Kraken affiliate, announced on July 29th that the team had signed defenseman Gustav Olofsson. slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>Montreal Canadiens’ defenseman Jayden Struble now has four years of professional hockey under his belt, but he has yet to establish himself as a full-time NHLer. For the last three seasons, he’s been in a duel with teammate Arber Xhekaj for the sixth defenseman role. Thanks to the injury bug, though, they’ve both seen a fair bit of action. Last year, Struble skated in 59 games with an average of 14:01 of ice time,

<<<INDENT>>>(cont) while Xhekaj saw action in 65 games but only averaged 11:25 of ice time. However, in the playoffs, Struble played in 12 games and averaged 11:40 of ice time, while Xhekaj played in 13 games but averaged only 8:06.
